name: Critical minerals
summary: China's rare-earth export-control pause expires 10 Nov with no renewal announced
state: China's one-year suspension of some rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov, and no renewal had been announced as of 3 Nov; lapsed controls would bring back tighter licensing. Helium supply for chipmakers remains tight with Qatari output stuck behind Hormuz. No production stoppages outside China have been confirmed, so the Alert line is not crossed.
for_you: Possible delays and higher prices for electronics, cars and other goods using rare-earth magnets.
rubric_hit: Licensing tightening risk; no stoppages = Watch

sources.title: FXStreet — China's rare-earth leverage has an expiration date: 10 Nov
Startup Fortune — Rare-earth truce expires 10 Nov with no renewal in sight

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
